thread:
maria.g: Hey team — customer reporting a flurry of 500s on hosted inference. They provided request_id `req_0a1b2c3d4e5f`. Region us-west-2, endpoint /v1/generate, model redwood-13b-v2. Happened ~2026-03-15T22:12:34Z. Can somebody locate server-side logs and confirm whether this is a runtime crash vs upstream timeout?

ajay: Thanks — can you confirm whether this was via the public API (api.redwood.ai) or a Dedicated/private endpoint? Also approximate client IP if they have it.

maria.g: Public API (api.redwood.ai). No client IP in ticket, only the request_id and customer stacktrace showing HTTP 500. Time window +/- 5m from the timestamp above.

samir: I'll try a quick KQL across our indices. Use this in Kibana Discover to find any hits by request id (search across runtime and edge indices):

```
// KQL / Lucene-ish query for Discover
request_id: "req_0a1b2c3d4e5f" OR trace.id: "req_0a1b2c3d4e5f"
@timestamp >= "2026-03-15T22:07:00Z" AND @timestamp <= "2026-03-15T22:17:00Z"
```

samir: If you get nothing in hot indices, run the same query against cold/cold-archived index patterns (logs-*-cold, logs-*-archive). If you need shard-level exports we can run an ES scroll and export the hits.

oncall-bot: FYI logs retention: hot indices 7d, warm 23d (total 30d). After 30d records move to cold archive and require an archive fetch request (see runbook: http://internal.runbooks/logs-retention).

katie: If we need to repro from the customer's side, ask them for a curl repro and the full request body they used. Quick reproducible curl to attach request_id (so server logs will include the same id) — they can set X-Request-Id or our request_id field depending on SDK: 

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c4e5f"
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"test","max_tokens":8}'
```

katie: Note: if they use our SDK the SDK may override X-Request-Id. Prefer they include the request_id in the top-level payload if possible so it appears in application logs.

ajay: Maria — I pulled the initial Discover hits (hot indices) and found an ERROR from runtime-worker (node: runtime-4) at 2026-03-15T22:12:36Z referencing that request_id. Sending snippet.

samir: Paste the log lines here (or attach debug bundle). If it's a native crash we'll need the core dump + container logs. If it's a 502/timeout from upstream, the logs will point to the upstream host.

maria.g: Pasting sanitized snippet from customer ticket: 
```
ERROR runtime: handler failed request_id=req_0a1b2c4e5f cause="kv cache miss and upstream timeout" upstream=10.12.5.22:4373 dur_ms=3012
```

ops-eng: That snippet suggests a backend HTTP timeout to an upstream service. Samir — can you map runtime-4 -> infra node id and check the kube pod logs + sidecar?

samir: On it. If folks need to fetch older logs beyond 30d, open an "archive retrieval" via #eng-infra with the index name and time range. For immediate handoff: I'm exporting the runtime worker pod logs for the 22:10-22:15 window and will upload to the ticket.

maria.g: Thanks. Also asked customer to run curl with request_id in header and to attach full request JSON + timing.

katie: To create a debug bundle from prod for this request_id: run internal tool `rb-debug collect --req req_0a1b2c3d4e5f --include=pod-logs,kernel,metrics` and attach the tar.gz to the Zendesk ticket. If they can't run that, we can generate server-side bundle and share a presigned link.

ajay: Uploads done — I attached exported log tarball to the ticket and included the KQL I ran. Initial triage: 5xx appears transient and correlated to a brief spike of upstream latencies. No core dumps.

maria.g: Great. I'll reply to the customer with the snippet + suggestion to retry and include repro curl. I'll keep the ticket open until we have the debug bundle attached. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: If anyone wants to followup with infra for capacity checks, tag #eng-infra and include the node id and pod name from the bundle.

maria.g: Closing loop here — marking this as "awaiting customer repro" and attaching our exported logs and the KQL to the ticket. Will reopen if we see additional hits. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
